body:
<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 58e1f06. CI builds, and the PR merges cleanly into main. Engines already behave this way: libxml2 and expat report an empty-element tag as a start event followed by an end event, so WebKit runs `finishParsingChildren()` and Gecko runs `DoneAddingChildren()` for `<video/>`. `<style/>` and `<object/>` still react to their insertion, because they're never on the stack of open elements. The HTML parser has the same gap for normal start tags, so that's now tracked in #13282 and needs nothing here.

**Suggestions**

- Consider spelling out ["if the parser successfully parsed the entire element"](https://github.com/JinDX/html/blob/58e1f06a4bafe5631b9a814e5a3be73f0886e68c/source#L153851). It has to exclude two cases: a well-formedness error, and the parser being aborted (abort a parser pops the whole stack, and the XML parser is aborted "in the same way as for an HTML parser"). A positive phrasing would be clearer, e.g. "if that happened because the element's end tag was parsed or because the element is represented by an empty-element tag".
- This is a normative change. As written today, `<video src=…/>` never clears its blocked-on-parser flag, so it never fires `loadedmetadata`, and `<script src=…/>` is never prepared. Consider restoring the PR template and adding a WPT test, e.g. an `.xhtml` test where `<video src=…/>` and `<audio src=…/>` fire `loadedmetadata`. Since implementations already match, no implementation bugs are needed.

**Nits**

- ["after creating the element and performing the corresponding tree operations"](https://github.com/JinDX/html/blob/58e1f06a4bafe5631b9a814e5a3be73f0886e68c/source#L153803) doesn't say which tree operations. "immediately after inserting it" would be more precise.
- The title's "XML parser completion" reads like it's about stop parsing. Maybe "Finish parsing the children of XML empty-element tags".

</details>
